avoid_for: Playful consumer brands, multi-color or light-mode contexts, editorial long-form reading, and any interface needing more than one bright accent or shadow-based depth — the cobalt single-action discipline and hushed premium darkness only work as dark, monochrome, and calm.
best_for: Fintech and premium banking landing pages, dark-mode developer tools, and product launches wanting cinematic aspiration — an onyx canvas, graphite cards, intermediate-weight typography, and one cobalt action button as the gravitational center.
name: Mercury
palette_voice: Near-black Onyx Canvas (#171721) sets a cinematic observatory atmosphere with Graphite Card (#1e1e2a) one step lighter for flat, borderless content surfaces; Ivory Text (#ededf3) is the dominant foreground with Ash (#c3c3cc) muted copy; a single vivid Cobalt (#5266eb) is the only chromatic note, reserved exclusively for the primary 'Open account' action — never decorative, never a secondary button; no shadows, separation purely via graphite-on-onyx value lift.
signature_moves: One Cobalt-filled pill button per page as the sole chromatic action — the gravitational center of the layout
Intermediate-weight typography (arcadiaDisplay at 480, not 600/700) — asserts without shouting, the signature restraint
Graphite cards (#1e1e2a, 12px radius, 32px padding) with no border and no shadow — the one-step value lift creates separation
Pill-shaped interactive controls (32–40px radius) with sharp 4px corners reserved for structural elements only
Transparent nav over the hero with backdrop-blur frosted-glass on scroll, plus a full-bleed photographic alpine hero

source.shadow: none — flat, value contrast between onyx and graphite

typographic_voice: Two custom faces — arcadia for body/UI and arcadiaDisplay for headlines — built on an intermediate weight axis (360/420/480/530) that avoids the bold/light binary: heading weight 480 is the ceiling, body stays 16px weight 400 with generous 1.5 line-height, and display uses tight 1.1–1.15 leading with positive 0.01–0.02em letter-spacing for a wide-set, architectural quality; never editorial, never corporate.
